edges.description: Absence of functional transporter protein directly abolishes MCT8-mediated cellular uptake of thyroid hormone.
Loss of MCT8-mediated transport across brain barriers and into neurons starves the CNS of thyroid hormone.
Blocked cellular uptake and altered peripheral deiodinase handling shift circulating iodothyronines toward high T3 with low free T4.
Thyroid hormone is the timing signal for oligodendrocyte precursor differentiation; without it, myelination is delayed.
T3-dependent programs governing neural-progenitor expansion, neuronal migration, and cortical maturation are under-driven.
Human CSF and treatment-response data link MCT8 deficiency to impaired dopamine metabolism, although the intervening molecular steps are not yet known.
The oligodendrocyte differentiation block manifests radiologically as a global delay in myelination.
Deficient myelination of corticospinal projections contributes to the pyramidal signs that supersede infantile hypotonia.
Combined hypomyelination of motor pathways and central motor under-development leaves most affected males unable to walk independently.
Failure of T3-dependent cortical development produces severe cognitive impairment.
Immature central motor control presents in infancy as truncal hypotonia and absent head control.
Altered neuronal development contributes to extrapyramidal movement abnormalities, but the responsible circuit and intermediate steps have not been established in patients.
Choreoathetoid posturing is part of the extrapyramidal phenotype, but its specific developmental circuit mechanism remains unresolved.
Severe global neurodevelopmental failure leaves most patients without speech.
Seizures occur in the neurological phenotype, but a specific cellular mechanism has not been demonstrated.
Immature bulbar and oromotor control produces infantile feeding difficulty and excessive drooling.
The same bulbar and oromotor deficit impairs swallowing, predisposing to aspiration.
Aspiration of food and secretions across an incompetent swallow produces the pulmonary infection that is the leading cause of death.
Central neurodevelopmental impairment is associated with nystagmus, but the responsible oculomotor circuit has not been resolved.
Truncal hypotonia, spasticity, and absent independent ambulation combine to produce neuromuscular scoliosis.
The same abnormal tone and absence of weight-bearing predispose to hip dysplasia and dislocation.

Reduced dopamine-pathway output manifests as hypokinesia, hypomimia, rigidity, dystonia, autonomic dysfunction, and impaired sitting or standing, with a favorable response to levodopa/carbidopa in most treated patients.

edges.description: The elevated circulating T3 is freely taken up by tissues that do not depend on MCT8, over-stimulating them.
The serum pattern is measured directly as elevated free and total T3.
Enhanced T4-to-T3 conversion lowers circulating free thyroxine.
TSH fails to fall as the elevated T3 would predict, because pituitary hormone sensing is itself partly MCT8-dependent.
The divergence of T3 and T4 raises the T3/T4 ratio, a derived diagnostic index.
The shift of peripheral deiodination away from the inactivating type 3 pathway lowers circulating reverse T3.
Excess T3 action in peripheral tissues raises metabolic rate and drives catabolism.
Negative energy balance from hypermetabolism produces poor weight gain.
Catabolic T3 excess in skeletal muscle drives muscle wasting.
Excess T3 action on MCT8-independent cardiac tissue raises resting heart rate.
The same unopposed atrial T3 action produces ectopic atrial automaticity and premature atrial contractions.
Increased cardiac output and reduced systemic vascular resistance from peripheral T3 excess raise systolic blood pressure.

nodes.description: Brain thyroid hormone content falls despite normal or elevated circulating T3, because MCT8 is the rate-limiting import step at the blood-brain barrier and in MCT8-dependent neurons. The CNS therefore behaves as a hypothyroid tissue: T3-responsive gene programs are under-driven, and compensatory deiodinase changes (increased DIO2, decreased DIO3) fail to restore local hormone supply. This is the one conserved step AHDS shares with classical hypothyroidism, and the only node here that declares module conformance.

nodes.description: Beyond myelin, thyroid hormone drives neural-progenitor expansion, neuronal migration, and cortical maturation. The long-term cohort shows a very low developmental ceiling, but does not by itself establish which neuronal subprogram accounts for each clinical manifestation.

nodes.description: MCT8 is a thyroid hormone-specific transporter that carries T3 and T4 across the plasma membrane. Its loss does not affect hormone synthesis or receptor function; it blocks hormone entry into cells. Critically, MCT8 dependence is tissue-selective. Brain barriers and many neurons rely on MCT8 as the rate-limiting import route, whereas liver, heart, and skeletal muscle import T3 through alternative transporters (MCT10, OATP family). This single lesion therefore partitions the body into hormone-deprived and hormone-overexposed compartments.

evidence.reference_title: Structural insights into brain thyroid hormone transport via MCT8 and OATP1C1.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report cryoelectron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of MCT8 and OATP1C1 bound with the active thyroid hormone triiodothyronine (T3) and the prohormone thyroxine (T4) at 2.9 and 2.3 Å resolutions, respectively. Combined with functional studies, we elucidate their distinct thyroid hormone recognition and transport mechanisms and explain disease mutations.

nodes.description: Liver, heart, kidney, and skeletal muscle import T3 through MCT10, OATP, and other non-MCT8 routes, so they are fully exposed to the elevated circulating T3. These tissues are therefore chronically thyrotoxic while the brain is hypothyroid. This is the mechanistic reason why levothyroxine or liothyronine replacement is harmful in AHDS: extra hormone cannot reach the brain but does reach and further over-stimulate the periphery.

nodes.description: The diagnostic biochemical triad is high serum T3 with low or low-normal free T4 and a normal or only mildly elevated TSH, giving an increased T3/T4 ratio and low reverse T3. This pattern arises because tissues that retain hormone uptake (notably liver) increase type 1 deiodinase activity, converting T4 to T3, while the pituitary and hypothalamus receive a mixed signal, so TSH is not suppressed to the degree the elevated T3 would predict. The combination is what distinguishes AHDS from ordinary primary hypothyroidism (low T3 and T4 with high TSH) and from thyroid hormone resistance syndromes, and it is the diagnostic key.

nodes.description: Triac (3,3',5-triiodothyroacetic acid, tiratricol) is a T3 analogue that binds the same thyroid hormone receptors as T3 but enters cells independently of MCT8. It is the rational therapy for AHDS: it suppresses the pituitary, lowering the elevated serum T3 and thereby relieving peripheral thyrotoxicosis, and can in principle reach MCT8-dependent tissues that T3 cannot. In the international phase 2 Triac Trial (46 patients), serum T3 fell from 4.97 to 1.82 nmol/L over 12 months with only transient adverse effects; a real-life cohort of 67 patients treated up to 6 years confirmed sustained benefit with gains in body weight, reductions in heart rate, and falling SHBG. Evidence that Triac reverses the cerebral hypothyroidism is much weaker than the evidence for peripheral benefit, and is the question Triac Trial II was designed to answer by treating boys aged 30 months or younger. Tiratricol received European Union approval in 2025 specifically for peripheral thyrotoxicosis in MCT8 deficiency from birth; this approval does not establish neurological efficacy.
